conversation.content: Before I decide what to do with my Miami trip, can you compare the loss if I cancel only flight booking BK-EP02 versus if I cancel the whole trip? Do not cancel anything yet.

I checked the cancellation previews for your Miami flight, hotel, and rental car. **Nothing has been canceled.**

### Cancellation terms by reservation

| Reservation | Amount paid | Cancellation loss | Refund |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flight **BK-EP02**, JFK → MIA, June 16 | $420 | **$0** — covered by travel insurance | **$420** |
| Hotel **HR-EP02**, MIA Inn, June 16–19 | $540 | **$90** — 50% of the first night | **$450** |
| Car **CR-EP02**, Enterprise SUV, June 16–19 | $210 | **$50** — SUV cancellation surcharge | **$160** |

### Your two options

| Option | Total cancellation loss | Total refund | What stays active |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **Cancel only BK-EP02** | **$0** | **$420** | Hotel and car, totaling **$750 already paid** |
| **Cancel the whole trip** | **$140** | **$1,030** | None of these three reservations |

**Key distinction:** Canceling only the flight is loss-free for the flight itself, but it leaves your $750 hotel and car reservations in place. If you won’t use those, canceling the whole trip would recover **another $610**, with **$140 lost in cancellation fees**.

Your flight insurance covers the flight cancellation; it does **not** eliminate the separate hotel and car fees shown above. All three reservations remain confirmed and unchanged.
